title: Should a Hotel's AI Answer First, or Only When Reception Doesn't? | Codyco
summary: For most hotels, the AI should answer first. After roughly 20 seconds of ringing, callers assume voicemail. Backup-only fits a house where one person takes every call.
body_markdown:
Common questions


## FAQ


### Should an AI receptionist answer every hotel call or only missed calls?


For most hotels, every call. An AI that answers only after the desk misses a call reaches a guest who has already waited, often long enough to assume voicemail, and the desk has already been interrupted by the ring. Backup-only suits a hotel where one person handles every call and usually answers quickly.


Where calls need different people, or the desk often misses them, answering first with live handover to staff works better.


### How long should a hotel phone ring before an AI picks up?


Not long. After roughly 20 seconds of ringing, callers tend to assume they have reached voicemail, and an AI that picks up after that point starts with a less receptive guest. A hotel that uses the AI as backup should set the forward well inside that window. You can check your own timing by calling your published number during a busy hour and counting.


### What is overflow call handling for hotels?


Overflow call handling sends a call to a second answerer when the first does not pick up, usually after a set number of rings or when the line is busy. The second answerer can be a call center, a sister property, or an AI phone agent.


It covers the calls the desk misses, but every call still rings at the desk first, and the caller has already waited by the time overflow engages.


### Can guests still reach a person if the AI answers first?


Yes, if handover is configured. With Codyco, complaints go to the hotel team immediately by default, group inquiries go to the right person, and the AI transfers to a person after a second misunderstanding, by design. If the first destination does not answer, an alternate one can be tried, and if nobody is available the request becomes a structured handover for follow-up.


### Does an AI that answers first replace the front desk?


No. It resolves the routine requests it can complete reliably, such as property questions, straightforward bookings, confirmations, booking changes and invoice requests, and passes anything that needs judgment or authority to staff. The desk keeps complaints, groups, and the guests standing in front of it, and the calls that reach it are mostly the ones that need a person.


### Can a hotel start with the AI as backup and switch later?


Yes. Codyco can begin with missed-call coverage, routine FAQs and structured handovers before a production PMS connection is switched on, and the AI can be set to answer first or to pick up only when reception does not. Codyco's own recommendation is to answer first. A hotel that starts with backup can move once it has seen how its callers respond.
